links.outcome: Physician decision accuracy with versus without GPT-4 assistance (pre-post) in chest pain vignettes
links.effect: Accuracy improved from 47% to 65% (white male patient) and 63% to 80% (Black female patient); improvement about 18% in both groups.
links.quote: The accuracy improvement occurs without introducing or exacerbating demographic biases, with both groups showing similar magnitudes of improvement (18%).

links.outcome: Differential effect of AI assistance on physician decisions by patient race and sex
links.effect: Both patient groups showed similar improvement magnitudes (18%) with no introduced or exacerbated demographic bias.
links.quote: The accuracy improvement occurs without introducing or exacerbating demographic biases, with both groups showing similar magnitudes of improvement (18%).

screen.reason: Empirical randomized study testing physician decision-making and demographic bias before and after receiving GPT-4 recommendations for standardized clinical vignettes.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinical decision making with physician in the loop
